questions.q: How many hours of focused work a day does the summary say produce the best results?
a: About four
About six
About eight
About ten
questions.why: Lesson 1 recommends four diligent hours, arguing they beat eight distracted ones.

questions.q: Why does the summary say working long hours backfires?
a: Your productivity drops the longer you keep going
Your employer stops noticing your effort
Your colleagues begin to resent you
Your creativity peaks after ten hours
questions.why: Lesson 1 reports that people working 60 hours were the least productive of all the groups studied.

questions.q: In the study described, what happened to students who were interrupted mid-task?
a: They came up with more creative uses for the paper
They finished the task much faster than the others
They forgot the original instructions entirely
They produced fewer and less original ideas
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes an experiment where the group that stepped away generated more creative answers.

questions.q: What does the summary say your brain does when you stop working on a problem?
a: It keeps processing the task subconsciously
It shuts down until you sit back down
It replays only the mistakes you made
It cannot focus again for the rest of the day
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that the mind continues to examine problems and produce ideas while you are away from them.

questions.q: What does the example of Winston Churchill illustrate?
a: That deep play can rescue you in a dark time
That leaders should work longer hours
That hobbies distract from serious work
That painting improves military strategy
questions.why: Lesson 3 says Churchill found oil painting therapeutic and credited it with helping him through a very dark period.
